description.narrative: IFC anticipates that the Project will catalyze financial inclusion for smallholder farmers and rural borrowers, demonstrating the effectiveness of the partnership model between financiers and Agtech companies. IFC anticipates that the Agri RSF will increase access to finance for farmers by providing Sterling with an efficient and competitive risk mitigating tool to accept a higher degree of lending risk. IFC anticipates that the RSF will enable the Bank to sustainably increase its agri-portfolio risk profile. The RSF is expected to help increase the availability of locally produced staple crops, increase access to fertilizers and contribute to food security in the context of high food inflation which threatens food security. Nigeria which relies on imports to meet its food and agricultural production shortfalls ranks 107th out of 113 countries in the Global Food Security Index. The facility will facilitate agricultural intensification in Nigeria through increase farmers access to finance for crop production and fertilizers import. The program expects to reach 73,000 hectares and 110,000 farmers with increased access to inputs, agri equipment, insurance, and markets, resulting in improved livelihood and productivity.

The proposed Project consists of a financing package of up to US$25 million (the Project) for Sterling Bank Limited (Sterling Bank or the Bank), comprised of the following: (i) a US$20 million Global Warehouse Finance Program (GWFP) facility to be processed under the Africa Trade and Supply Chain Recovery Initiative (ATRI); and (ii) an unfunded agri Risk Sharing Facility (RSF) of up to US$5 million (equivalent in Naira) on a US$10 million (equivalent in Naira) portfolio of farmers to be originated through a partnership with Babban Gona (BG), an agricultural technology company (AgTech) in Nigeria for the benefit of maize smallholder farmers (SHFs) in its network. IFC will provide advisory services support on the use of the agri-RSF by the Bank. The RSF would be processed under IFCs Small Loans Guarantee Program European Commission/Private Sector Window (SLGP EC/PSW or the Program), a programmatic approach to risk sharing which aims to enhance and strengthen the capacity of financial institutions for risk taking and financing of MSMEs in eligible countries.
